Draw a Sprott 7e attractor straight to a PNG file.

Source: R/png.R
png_sprott_7e.Rd

Orbit, binning, colouring and PNG encoding all run in Rust, which makes this the fast route to large images, for example for print. The PNG uses fast compression with no row filter, which trades a larger file for speed.

Usage

png_sprott_7e(
  a,
  filename = "attractor.png",
  n = 1e+07,
  x0 = 1,
  y0 = 1,
  size = c(3840, 2160),
  gradient = "turbo",
  qs = 0.075,
  parallel_orbit = default_parallel_orbit()
)

Arguments

a

Numeric vector of length 14

filename

Output file name.

n

Number of points to generate

x0

Initial value for x

y0

Initial value for y

size

Image size in pixels, c(width, height).

gradient

Gradient name: one of "turbo", "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", or a ColorBrewer name such as "BuPu", "Oranges", "Reds", "Greens", "Blues", "BuGn", "Spectral" or "PuOr".

qs

quantile cutoff, a single number in [0, 0.5)

parallel_orbit

Number of parallel orbit trajectories (one per thread by default); 1 for the serial orbit

Value

The file name, invisibly.

See also

Other sprott functions: attractor_sprott_7e(), seed_sprott_7e()

Examples

a <- seed_sprott_7e(fast_forward = 429)
f <- png_sprott_7e(a, tempfile(fileext = ".png"), n = 1e6, size = c(400, 300))
